belief: I must be the strong one, no matter what.
origins: The oldest child, the caregiver, the spouse who “keeps it together,” or the one who learned early that no one else would. Others depend on us, and we feel we have no right to fall apart. Over time, exhaustion, resentment, and isolation build.
teaches: Paul says, “My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is perfected in weakness.” “Cast your burden upon the LORD and He will sustain you.” “Come to Me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.” “Carry one another’s burdens.” Moses needed Aaron and Hur to hold up his arms. We are not meant to be the source of strength for everyone. God is. Our job is to lean on Him and let others share the load.
self_statements: If I fall apart, everything falls apart.
No one else can handle this.
I do not get to be weak.
I have to hold it together.
errors: Believing I am either strong or a failure.
Assuming others cannot cope without me.
Feeling needed and concluding that I cannot stop.
questions: When did I first become “the strong one”?
What would really happen if I rested or asked for help?
Who could share some of the load?
What does God say about being sustained?
What have I lost by never leaning?
What is one thing I can hand off?
truth: God is the strong one. I can cast my burdens on Him, let others share the load, and rest. My weakness is not the end of the world. It is where His power is seen.
hw_truths: His power is perfected in weakness.
Jesus gives rest to the weary.
log: Each week, note one load you shared or handed off.
actions: Ask someone to take one task.
prayer: Lord, I have been the strong one for too long. I cast my burdens on You. Sustain me, and send people to share the load. Amen.
name_example: Sarah can write: “I will cast my burden on the Lord and He will sustain me.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “I must be the strong one, no matter what.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
